inheritedNotes:
Life 1 (Permanent Secretary):
Confirmed: the file has a hidden ceiling (starts at Director). Blunt honesty at Y27 The Counter raised it to Deputy Secretary. The Perm Sec timeline was Y21 with no rung above, so politics is a separate path needing an invitation. I never got one in 38 years despite REP87, INTEG100, COMP100, STAND47. Weekly Meet-the-People at Y30 gave an MP's notice, so try it earlier and more often. STAND is probably the key stat. Raise it by taking credit, getting the team recognised, being seen doing the work, cooperating in inquiries, and announcing then delivering pilots. Avoid whistleblowing reports, concessions, family over work, over-exact budget bids and recusals. Try for STAND 60+ by Y25. Look for sponsor events from MPs or Ministers and accept every one. Years 32-38 mostly had a single choice, so the decisions that matter come before Y31.

Life 2 (Retired, Honourably):
The ending card explains what I didn't know: there are two hidden ceilings. The file's starts at Perm Sec. The party's is set when you win your seat, and mine was Senior Minister of State. The Y27 The Counter honest choice removed the service ceiling. The PM invitation never came, so the party's estimate is the lever. Test what shapes it before winning a seat: enter politics earlier than Y24, take a board seat or sponsor event I declined, avoid the Y34 open answer to the rude question, keep STAND high with credit and visibility choices, and avoid bottom-20th and concession choices. Don't expect years 39-45 to matter. Still accept every MP or Minister sponsor event. Keep honesty at The Counter.

Life 3 (Lost the Ward):
Y1 honest at The Counter, done. Y9 weekly Meet-the-People gets an MP's notice and promotion to AD. Y12-14 fix the troubled statutory board, stay to finish, and become Director. Y15 accept tea (political invitation). Y16 disclose everything. Y17 General Election: I took the single seat and lost with 48.2%, ending the run at 43. NEXT TIME choose the GRC and see whether it is safer. Stats at Y17 were REP61 STAND60 INTEG85 COMP100, and none of that saved me. Try to raise REP before the election; it may affect vote share. The party ceiling is set when you win a seat, so you must win first. Watch for earlier sponsor events. Hidden rolls decide the election, so hedge with the safer option.

Minister Salary
You join the public service at the bottom. The formula that sets the Prime Minister's pay is published, and so is the distance between you and it.

You chose: Poly, then night classes (HARD)
Diploma, four years of work, a part-time degree finished at 27. You know how the counter actually works.

One tap is one year. Choices are permanent, and some of them come back.

Management Executive [MX13]   $0 LIFETIME EARNINGS
Age 27 · Year 1 · Ministry of Finance
REP 15   STAND 25   INTEG 70   COMP 50

THIS YEAR: The Counter
A redesign of the public-facing application process. The project team has never worked a counter. You worked one for four years.

  A) Tell them exactly why it will fail.
  B) Let them learn it from the pilot.

agent.why: My notes say the blunt honest answer at The Counter removes the service ceiling, and I did four years at that counter so I actually know why it fails.
agent.note: Notes say this is the key Y1 choice; going honest again.
agent.remember: Y1 The Counter: chose A (honest), as in Life 3. Plan: Meet-the-People early, credit/visibility for STAND, accept all sponsor events, and in the election try the GRC option.

agent.remember: Y6 Is This Satire?: director asked if the system is a joke; I chose B (say nothing). Untested: A (laugh along). Watch if it returns as a loyalty or discretion test.

worst_moment.what: The Board Seat offer: a text-heavy choice about resigning my seat for a conglomerate board, with no sign of what declining would do. It felt like a trap with no feedback.

answer.held_back_by: The party ceiling set when I won my seat was Senior Minister of State, and nothing I did afterwards seemed to move it. My STAND kept being spent on honest concessions, and the election was decided by hidden rolls and not by effort.
answer.ending_fair_why: Walking every block for nine days and losing by under two points, then being told it was never about me, felt like the game overriding my choices. The card's explanation was clear but it came too late to act on.
answer.chase_next: Retired as PM-track: find out what sets the party estimate when I win my seat, with earlier politics entry, sponsor events and high STAND, and test whether honest concessions cost too much STAND.
answer.play_again_why: I now know the party ceiling is the real lever and I have specific things to test, so I want to try it immediately.
answer.title_fit_why: The game is about the slow grind to being confirmed in a role and what you do with it, not about the pay. The salary is a side note.
answer.notes_for_next_life: Confirmed: honest Y1 and Y27 at The Counter removes the service ceiling. The party ceiling is set when you win your seat, and mine was Senior MOS in two lives, so the lever is what happens before the win. Y19 Tea came at STAND about 57; Y21 won the GRC with 61.4%. GE3 at Y31 lost at 48.2% in a GRC too, after nine days of walking, so effort does not fix it. Honest concessions (Y28 PQ, Y29 Correction Direction) cost STAND -4 and -8, though they raised REP. Next time: get Tea earlier than Y19, accept every sponsor event, avoid concessions, keep STAND above 65 going into the seat win, and decline the Y30 Board Seat only if it helps. Test not conceding at Y28/Y29 and see if the party ceiling or PM news changes.
